HELLO, GOODBYE
A few weeks ago, Alessio Dionisi was forced to deny the “fake news” he had joined Sean Dyche, Gianfranco Zola, Beppe Sannino, Óscar García, Billy McKinlay, Slavisa Jokanovic, Quique Sánchez Flores (twice), Walter Mazzarri, Marco Silva, Javi Gracia (twice), Nigel Pearson, Vladimir Ivic, Xisco Muñoz, Claudio Ranieri, Roy Hodgson, Rob Edwards, Slaven Bilic, Chris Wilder, Valérien Ismael, Tom Cleverley, Paulo Pezzolano and Edward Still in being sacked by the Pozzo family since 2012. There was no denial on Sunday, when the axe inevitably fell on the head coach following a 4-0 shellacking at Sheffield United and the Italian left after only 18 games in charge. While his reign is unlikely to live long in the memory of anyone at Vicarage Road, Dionisi can at least boast on his LinkedIn page that in terms of longevity under the Pozzos, he took charge of 18 more matches than Dyche, 17 more than García and 16 more than McKinlay. Indeed, he even outlasted Rob Edwards, who was assured he would be backed “come hell or high water” upon his 2022 appointment, only to be fired from the ejector seat 11 games later.
It’s been quite the white-knuckle ride for Watford since the Pozzos arrived, armed only with a spreadsheet, an army of Udinese cast-offs and knowledge of the loophole that there was no Football League cap on the number of players who could be brought in on loan from clubs outside the UK. And while few fans will be able to recall all 25 of the coaches who have been hired and fired by the Pozzos, they do have fond memories to take to the grave. There was that end-to-end Troy Deeney play-off semi-final goal against Leicester. There were five uninterrupted seasons in the Premier League. There was that time they ended Liverpool’s 44-match unbeaten Premier League run despite being stuck in the relegation zone. And what self-respecting Hornet will ever forget travelling to watch their team play in the 2019 FA Cup final?
Of course it hasn’t all been rosy in the Pozzo garden. The eight-day managerial reign of McKinlay was a source of much mirth for fans of rival clubs. A double relegation from the Premier League – the first amid allegations of a dressing-room bust-up linked to an illegal lockdown party – wasn’t great either. Playing I’m Still Standing by Elton John, the club’s honorary life president, over the Vicarage Road PA system to mark their descent into the Championship heaped further embarrassment upon the club. And what self-respecting Hornet will ever forget travelling home after watching their team play in the 2019 FA Cup final?
While it would be foolish to predict what will happen next at a club that currently sit two places above the Championship relegation zone, the one stonewall certainty is that the name “Edward Iordanescu” will be the next to be copied and pasted into the over-worked club template announcing a managerial departure. The Romanian was formally introduced this morning and with this being his 14th job in the past 16 years, he can arguably lay claim to being the most ‘Watford’ manager of the Pozzo era. “For me, I want a team that plays very good, organised football with the spirit and attitude, and the strong mentality,” he blathered, as local reporters dabbed their bingo cards. “And then, yes, regarding the organisation of the team, that takes time.” History suggests getting the time he needs is a pipe dream for Iordanescu, whose first game in charge is away at Championship basement-dwellers Derby County. Should Watford go to Pride Park and lose, he could be out of a job by Saturday night.
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE
Join Scott Murray from 8pm for red-hot updates on Nottingham Forest 0-0 Chelsea in the Premier League.
QUOTE OF THE DAY
“I know people expect me to say: ‘Oh, I regret it.’ No, I don’t regret it. If I regret something, it’s that I would love to kick him in another [place]. The kung fu kick was criticised a lot, especially by journalists. But now it’s a [more positive] symbol. So I change everything” – Eric Cantona is in scintillating form during this chat with Donald McRae.
FOOTBALL DAILY LETTERS
 
 If you’ve never tried listening to or watching the utter drivel that is ‘The Overlap’, this will mean nothing whatsoever, but if you have, this, by the great Jonathan Liew, is absolutely superb. Satire so biting it even surpasses Luis Suárez at his 2010, 2013 and 2014 peaks” – Noble Francis.
 
 I read your depressing piece about Burnley (yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition). I am in the unfortunate position of being a season ticket holder at Turf Moor and residing in south-east London. A typical Saturday home game starts for me at 6am, involves two train journeys, the underground and a bus ride (that’s each way) getting home about midnight. Then there is the travel and food costs which are usually in the three figures. Evening games, like Wednesday, involve two days and a friend’s spare room. As a 70-year-old is it too much to expect a similar effort from those overpaid prancing show ponies that think they are too good for Burnley, too good for the Championship – if it’s only just for two hours on match day? There, I’ve said it and I feel much better. That is , of course, until 5pm on Saturday” – Chris Harrison.
If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Chris Harrison. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

מועדון הכדורגל ואטפורד נפרד ממאמנו אלסיו דיוניסי בעקבות תבוסה לעבר שפילד יונייטד, המצטרפת לשורת חילופי מאמנים ארוכה תחת הבעלות של משפחת פוצו מאז שנת 2012. דיוניסי עזב את תפקידו לאחר 18 משחקים בלבד שבהם עמד על הקווים.

במקומו של דיוניסי, מינתה ההנהלה את אדוארד יורדאנסקו הרומני לתפקיד המאמן. יורדאנסקו, שעבד ב-14 מקומות שונים בשנים האחרונות, צפוי לערוך את משחקו הראשון מול קבוצת התחתית דרבי קאונטי.
